title: Motion Verbs 1: идти vs ходить
description: The first motion-verb pair: walking. идти marks a single one-way trip in progress; ходить marks a round-trip, a habit, or a general ability.
descriptionRussian: Первая пара глаголов движения: пешком. Идти — однонаправленное движение в процессе. Ходить — туда и обратно, привычка или общая способность.
intro: Russian has no single verb meaning 'to go'. It has pairs, and the choice between the halves is not about tense or aspect but about the shape of the trip: one is a single journey underway in one direction, the other is a round trip, a habit, or a general fact. English buries that distinction in context. Russian puts it in the verb, and you have to pick before you speak.
rules: Идти = a single one-way trip in motion: underway now, one direction, one occasion. Present: иду, идёшь, идёт, идём, идёте, идут. Past: шёл / шла / шло / шли (irregular).
Ходить = round-trip, habit, or general ability. Present: хожу, ходишь, ходит, ходим, ходите, ходят. Past: ходил / ходила / ходило / ходили (regular -ил).
Cues that pull идти: сейчас, потом, скоро, a single destination on a single trip, a moment-of-motion frame ('когда я шёл').
Cues that pull ходить: часто, обычно, каждый день, иногда, по + dative time (по выходным), a finished past round-trip ('вчера ходил в магазин').
Both verbs go on foot; пешком (on foot) pairs with either, but never with ехать or ездить.
examples: Сейчас я иду в школу. (Right now I am going to school.) Идти: in-progress one-way trip.
Я хожу в школу каждый день. (I go to school every day.) Ходить: habit.
Антон ходил в парк вчера. (Anton went to the park yesterday and came back.) Ходить past: round-trip.
Когда Маша шла домой, она встретила Лену. (While Masha was walking home, she met Lena.) Идти past: motion in progress.
Лена часто ходит в музей. (Lena often goes to the museum.) Ходить with 'часто': habit.
Я иду пешком: магазин рядом. (I'm walking on foot; the store is close.) Идти: a single trip in progress.

tables.title: Motion on Foot: One-Way vs Round-Trip / Habit

items.promptEnglish: Right now Masha is going to school.
items.hint: Right now, in progress, one direction. Which verb signals motion happening at this moment?
items.explanation: 'Сейчас' (right now) anchors the action to the present moment as a single one-way trip in progress. Идёт = 3sg of идти. The form ходит would describe a regular habit ('she goes to school'), which the present-moment cue rules out.

items.promptEnglish: Anton goes to the park every Sunday.
items.hint: Каждое воскресенье is a habit cue. Which member of the pair handles repeated trips?
items.explanation: 'Каждое воскресенье' (every Sunday) is a frequency cue: the trip repeats. Repetition is the work of ходить, 3sg ходит. The form идёт would describe a single one-way trip in progress, not a weekly pattern.

items.prompt: Вчера Лена _____ в магазин и купила хлеб.
items.promptEnglish: Yesterday Lena went to the store (and came back) and bought bread.
items.hint: A past trip there AND back is a round-trip. Which past form covers both legs?
items.explanation: The past round-trip (Lena went to the store and returned) is the core ходить past meaning. Fem -ла: ходила. The form шла (past of идти) describes the moment of motion only ('she was walking'), not the completed there-and-back trip framed by 'вчера'.

items.prompt: Когда я _____ домой, я встретил старого друга.
items.promptEnglish: While I (m) was walking home, I met an old friend.
items.hint: 'When I was walking home' frames a moment within a single one-way trip. Past masc?
items.explanation: 'Когда я шёл домой' = 'while I was walking home': a moment captured inside a single in-progress one-way trip. Past masc of идти: шёл (irregular). The form ходил would describe a completed there-and-back trip, which cannot host the meeting that interrupts the motion.

items.promptEnglish: The kids walk to school (as a regular routine).
items.hint: A general statement about how the kids commute, not a single trip happening now. Habit?
items.explanation: The sentence describes how the kids regularly get to school, not what they are doing at this moment. Habit → ходить, 3pl ходят. Идут would mean they are walking to school right now, this single trip, which the general framing rules out.

items.prompt: Маша обычно _____ в кафе по выходным.
items.promptEnglish: Masha usually goes to the café on weekends.
items.hint: Обычно and по выходным are both habit cues. Which verb pairs with them?
items.explanation: Both 'обычно' (usually) and 'по выходным' (on weekends) mark a recurring pattern. Habit + repetition → ходить, 3sg ходит. Идти cannot host habit cues: it describes one trip on one occasion, not a routine.

hints: я: the trap form. The д turns into ж, so it is not «ходю»
explanations: хожу: 1sg of ходить. This is the only form where д becomes ж. «Ходю» does not exist.
ходишь: 2sg of ходить. Every form except the 1sg keeps ход-: ходишь, ходит, ходим, ходите, ходят.
ходят: 3pl of ходить: ход- + -ят, the 2nd-conjugation ending, never «ходют».

sentenceBuilding.translation: Right now I am going to school.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Frame: сейчас (now) + я + present of идти + destination. The cue 'сейчас' forces the one-way verb.

sentenceBuilding.answer: Каждый день Антон ходит на работу.
sentenceBuilding.translation: Every day Anton goes to work.
acceptableVariants: Каждый день Антон ходит на работу
Антон ходит на работу каждый день.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Frame: каждый день (every day) + name + present of ходить + destination. The habit cue forces the round-trip verb.

sentenceBuilding.translation: The children often go to the park.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Frame: subject + часто (often) + present of ходить (3pl) + destination. 'Часто' is a habit cue.

sentenceBuilding.answer: Когда Лена шла домой, она пела.
sentenceBuilding.translation: While Lena was walking home, she was singing.
acceptableVariants: Когда Лена шла домой, она пела
sentenceBuilding.hint: Frame: когда (while) + name + past of идти (fem) + destination, then the second clause. A moment inside one trip forces the one-way verb.

blanks: Я _____ в магазин каждое утро. (I (m) go to the store every morning.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: 'Каждое утро' (every morning) is a habit cue: the trip repeats. Habit → ходить, 1sg хожу. Иду would describe a single one-way trip happening at this moment, which the daily-routine frame rules out.

errorCorrection.sentence: Не звони мне сейчас: я хожу на важную встречу.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Don't call me right now: I'm on my way to an important meeting.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'Сейчас' anchors a single one-way trip in progress, which is the job of идти: иду. The round-trip хожу describes a habit ('I regularly attend important meetings'), which clashes with 'сейчас' and a single specific meeting. Choose идти for one trip happening now, ходить for routines and round-trips.

errorCorrection.sentence: Каждую субботу я иду в бассейн.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Every Saturday I go to the swimming pool.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'Каждую субботу' (every Saturday) is a frequency cue: the trip repeats, which is the work of the round-trip ходить: хожу. The one-way иду describes one trip happening right now, in one direction, which a weekly habit is not.

errorCorrection.sentence: Вчера мы шли в музей и вернулись поздно вечером.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Yesterday we went to the museum and came back late in the evening.
errorCorrection.explanation: The frame 'вчера ... и вернулись' (yesterday ... and came back) describes a completed there-and-back trip, which is the round-trip ходить past: ходили. The one-way шли captures only a moment of motion in one direction, not the whole round trip.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I (m) am going to the library right now.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'Сейчас' (right now) forces a present-moment in-progress reading: single one-way trip → идти, 1sg иду. Хожу would describe a habit (regular library trips), which the present-moment cue rules out.

minimalPairs.context: Я _____ в кафе три раза в неделю.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I (m) go to a café three times a week.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'Три раза в неделю' (three times a week) is a frequency cue: repetition → ходить, 1sg хожу. Иду would describe a single one-way trip happening at this moment, which the recurring-pattern frame rules out.

reviewVocab.definition: to go on foot, one-way and in progress (single trip happening at the reference moment, in one direction)
to go on foot, round-trip or habit or general ability (repeated trips, completed there-and-back, or the capacity to walk)
reviewVocab.example: Антон ходит на работу пешком каждый день.

reviewVocab.definition: on foot (the adverb that flags motion on foot; pairs with идти or ходить, never with ехать or ездить)
reviewVocab.example: Я хожу в магазин пешком: он близко.
